_comment: Drop-in hooks block for the consumer project's
.claude/settings.json. The PostToolUse and Stop hooks are
mandatory; SessionStart is gated on user opt-in during adoption
(omit if declined).
All commands reference ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR} so they work
regardless of where Claude Code was invoked from.
The SessionStart hook compares the local submodule HEAD against
the latest released tag at origin via `git ls-remote --tags`,
which queries the remote without modifying the local clone.
If the local pin is not at the latest released tag, the hook
outputs an explicit relay instruction to stdout, which Claude
Code captures as model context. The wrapper text instructs the
model to surface the message verbatim to the user at the start
of its first response.
Why not use stderr or exit 2? Both were tried in 0.2.4 and
neither produced user-visible output: SessionStart is a
non-blocking hook event in Claude Code, so stderr is not
displayed in the user's terminal and exit code 2 has no
effect. The model-relay approach is the documented
user-visibility channel that actually works for SessionStart.
The `http.lowSpeedLimit`/`http.lowSpeedTime` settings bound
session-start latency to about 3 seconds on a stalled network.
Offline failures stay silent via `|| exit 0` guards on each
step.

hooks.command: bash -c 'cd "${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}/.java-coding-standards" 2>/dev/null || exit 0; head_sha=$(git rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null) || exit 0; tags_raw=$(git -c http.lowSpeedLimit=1000 -c http.lowSpeedTime=3 ls-remote --tags origin 2>/dev/null); [ -n "$tags_raw" ] || exit 0; latest=$(echo "$tags_raw" | awk -F/ "{print \$NF}" | grep -v "\^{}$" | sort -V | tail -1); [ -n "$latest" ] || exit 0; latest_sha=$(echo "$tags_raw" | awk "\$2==\"refs/tags/${latest}^{}\" || \$2==\"refs/tags/${latest}\" {print \$1}" | tail -1); [ "$head_sha" = "$latest_sha" ] && exit 0; current=$(echo "$tags_raw" | awk -v h="$head_sha" "\$1==h {n=\$2; sub(\"\\\\^{}\",\"\",n); sub(\"refs/tags/\",\"\",n); print n}" | sort -V | tail -1); printf "INSTRUCTION FOR ASSISTANT (from SessionStart hook): At the start of your first response, tell the user verbatim: \"Heads up: .java-coding-standards has a newer release available (%s); current pin is %s. Run /init-java to refresh.\"\n" "$latest" "${current:-untagged}"'
